challenge.description: A new model version requires loyalty basket data, but the deployment pipeline lacks the governance controls to verify consent. #automation_alex# wants to push the automated deployment forward immediately to meet the promotion deadline, while #requirements_reuben# insists on a manual review process to ensure legal compliance. #automation_alex# is open to adding a manual approval step if it keeps the pipeline moving, but #requirements_reuben# will not accept any automated path without full audit trails.

output.content: I need the canary test to trigger automatically the moment a new model version is registered. Waiting for a manual request means the promotion week starts with an untested model, which is a risk I want to eliminate. The more automated coverage we have before the order window opens, the safer the deployment is for the stores. I am open to adding a manual approval step if it keeps the pipeline moving, but I want the test run itself to be fully automated. The sooner we catch a bad model, the better off we are when the leaflet goes out.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that increasing automated coverage makes the deployment safer and that catching bad models sooner is better, indicating that doing more than the minimum asked (full automation) would make them happier.
